lines.intro: Every morning I write a to-do list that is longer than my day. Dayspan turns the work day into an object you can hold, so the overflow shows up before nine a.m.
lines.enter: Your hours become a span in front of you. Every task is a tile, as long as the time it takes.
lines.place: Pinch a tile in the tray and drop it on the span. Everything after it slides aside.
lines.stretch: To resize, hold the tile with both hands and pull. Fifteen minutes is three point four centimeters, the same scale as the ruler.
lines.fill: Keep filling the day. Past the pink flag, tiles tip over the edge, and the panel counts the overtime.
lines.putback: Now the choice is right in front of you. The gym goes back in the tray, and the day fits.
lines.lock: Poke Lock day. The plan is saved, and today's ring appears.
lines.done: During the day, a quick pinch on a tile marks it done.
lines.next: Next morning, unfinished tiles come back with a notch for every day they were pushed.
lines.mr: In passthrough, Dayspan uses plane detection to find your real desk, and sets the tray down on it. Here the emulator's synthetic room stands in for a real one.
lines.outro: Dayspan. Hands only, seated, about ten minutes. Built with the Immersive Web SDK, running in the Quest browser.
